ranked_proposals.title: Remove auxiliary losses specifically during frozen-trunk head fine-tuning
ranked_proposals.hypothesis: Auxiliary structure and next-change losses help representation learning, but can constrain the final shared readout when the input projection and GRUs are already frozen. Main-only head tuning may improve the pooled correlation objective without new serving work. This is a testable optimization hypothesis, not an established explanation of the plateau.

concrete_gap.fact: The head-only gcorr stage still sets aux-struct=0.3 and aux-next=0.3; lines 20-21 freeze inp,gru.
All output heads share Linear(2H,H) then GELU before the final output matrix. Auxiliaries still backpropagate through this shared head.
Both auxiliary losses are unconditionally added at their fixed coefficients, then summed gradients are clipped at norm 1 at line 1078.

Output dimension and auxiliary offsets depend on auxiliary flags. Setting existing CLI flags to zero directly would change checkpoint shape; preserve heads and add separate fine-tune loss multipliers.

closest_existing_results: E-097/E-102 support auxiliary next-change learning in parent training; retain that successful parent recipe.
E-148/E-171 and current head-only versus full-FT comparisons change frozen parameters or the main objective, not whether auxiliary losses remain active within the same head-only stage.
E-107/E-233/E-237/E-244/E-251 add auxiliary targets; E-222 changes EMA consistency weighting. They do not test withdrawing existing auxiliary objectives only after trunk freezing.
E-180 running normalization was flat; this proposal changes the direction/objective of shared-head gradients, not merely their common scale.

cheap_discriminating_probe.status: Prepared concept; not authorized as an extra screen under the current one-family Transformer contract.
cheap_discriminating_probe.name: Training-side shared-head gradient audit
cheap_discriminating_probe.inputs: Fixed epoch3 parents ref_f0/ref_f1 and their logged head-FT recipes. Both model_ep3.pt paths exist remotely. Hash checkpoints, logs, selected chain IDs, data/split identities and code before gradients.
cheap_discriminating_probe.sample: For each fold take exactly 8 eligible head-FT training sequences, 2 per market class, selected by a fixed hash of chain ID; exclude the target held-out fold and mixed train-neighbour chains. Carry trunk state from sequence start. Evaluate fixed 512-row windows beginning at 2000, 8000, 16000. Freeze this selection before any gradients; no outcome-dependent replacement.
cheap_discriminating_probe.calculation: On head parameters compute separate gradients of gcorr and 0.3*L_struct+0.3*L_next using the existing masks/labels. Report per-fold cosine similarity and auxiliary/main norm ratio specifically on the shared first head layer; report global clipping factors descriptively. Also report zero/nonfinite gradients and all prespecified windows, not a selected negative slice.
cheap_discriminating_probe.decision: Use signs and auxiliary/main gradient norms to refine the optimization rationale. Do not require negative cosine as a hard pass gate: Adam, finite steps, regularization and checkpoint-versus-training-state differences can break that inference. A null audit weakens this explanation but cannot veto the controlled head-FT comparison. The candidate/control WP study below is the actual allocation test.
cheap_discriminating_probe.limits: This measures a frozen EMA parent under training-side batches, not historical optimizer trajectories. The epoch checkpoint does not save Adam state (train_rnn.py:1125); Euclidean cosines do not reconstruct preconditioned Adam updates. No WP or hidden-period improvement is claimed from gradients.
cheap_discriminating_probe.timeout_policy: 480 seconds is a hard stop, not a forecast of sequential GRU speed. If replay or gradients cannot finish, record timeout, processed chain IDs and incomplete coverage; do not shrink windows, reset state, select a faster checkpoint or interpret a partial score after inspection.

preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.candidate: Original four-epoch parent unchanged. Same one-epoch head-only gcorr fit, lr5e-4, batch16, exact data order, masks, chunk length, scheduler, initial weights and output dimensions; multiply structure and next-change fine-tune losses by zero. Keep inp/gru frozen. No full-FT stage.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.control: Same exact head-only fit with both loss multipliers 1 (current .3/.3 auxiliaries). Match optimizer parameter groups and random/data seeds. Verify historical control equivalence before using a cached control; otherwise regenerate the control within the stated budget.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.checkpoint_rule: Fixed parent epoch3 and head epoch0. No best-epoch selection, auxiliary weight sweep, schedule sweep or checkpoint interpolation.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.primary: All paired seed effects in exact pooled clipped |y|-weighted Pearson over pure scoring chains; report fold0, fold1 and pooled, then mean and sample SD across paired seeds.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.serving_relevance: For each seed separately replace the corresponding plain-h128 slot in the same C proxy with its main-only FT child, holding other members and .25 blend weights fixed. Also report one fixed replacement of both plain slots by the two candidates. No blend weight search.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.uncertainty: Whole-chain paired bootstrap for fixed-artifact metric deltas, distinct from across-seed variability; all results discovery-only. Do not present two seeds or reused folds as prospective confirmation.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.allocation_gate: Continue only if mean paired single-model effect is positive, both seed effects have positive pooled sign, and the fixed both-slot replacement improves pooled C by >=0.0003 with positive signs in both folds. This is a preallocated spending threshold reflecting near-zero serving cost, not significance, a guaranteed public gain or a global rejection of auxiliary learning.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.stop: One candidate recipe; on failure close this exact head-only intervention. No automatic public submission.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.implementation: Add an auxiliary LOSS-scale option independent of head construction, default 1, multiplying the existing structure/next-change contributions only. Candidate sets it to 0; control retains 1. Do not change --aux-struct=.3 or --aux-next=.3, output dimensions or optimizer parameter groups. Keep clip_grad_norm_=1, weight decay, scheduler, and EMA flags exactly equal to the original head-FT control; log their actual values. No such implementation was made in this scout.

cost.serving: Zero added state, parameters, MACs or native operators; identical model shapes and main outputs. Exact new weight parity still requires existing export tests.
cost.training: Four candidate head-only fits (2 seeds x 2 folds), plus controls only if historical equivalence fails. Frozen trunk still costs forward passes. Price the actual logged head-FT time before allocation; no invented GPU-hour estimate.

ranked_proposals.main_risk: The auxiliaries may regularize the shared readout even with a frozen trunk. Removing them may overfit the already reused valid masks or improve singles without contributing to C.
ranked_proposals.source_scope: Du et al., sections 2-3 and 6: fixed auxiliary weights can become unhelpful and gradient alignment is a local heuristic. It supplies motivation for the diagnostic, not evidence that this competition intervention succeeds.

ranked_proposals.title: Decode the auxiliary recurrence clock into actual bid/ask movement
ranked_proposals.status: Conditional architecture proposal; preflight only before any model allocation
ranked_proposals.hypothesis: A sparse event branch may be spending its updates on encoded book-shape transitions instead of price-moving quote events. Changing only that branch clock could preserve relevant event memory with the same state width. This does not establish extra information; the row GRU already observes the source features.

implementation_evidence.fact: DualClockModel and EventAttnModel both receive the same EV_I0PX input flag.
EV_I0PX is an AND of changes in the first encoded bid and ask price coordinates (line 48), not a decoded ask/bid-move test and not literally any-of-22.
learn_moves maps previous/current full 22-code pairs to modal (delta ask,delta bid), learned from target jumps in supplied training sequences.
The builder uses 1500 class-3 TRAIN sequences for move/spread tables when the cache is absent (lines 67-71). Existing-cache provenance must still be verified.
The matured-label correction failed a leakage check because code changes include shape-only events; honest quote-clock reconstruction removed its apparent gain.

ranked_proposals.closest_negative: H-020/E-056 and current R6 are direct negatives for a dual-clock GRU with the current proxy clock. Event attention, E-240 seasonal 12-lag readout, E-242 duration residual correction and E-251 future quote-path auxiliary are also cautionary. The narrow change is the event recurrence update mask, not another generic memory module or a future-label input.
ranked_proposals.causal_candidate: Use an immutable train-fitted map of (previous,current) 22-code tuples. If lookup is known, update the event GRU iff decoded delta ask != 0 OR delta bid != 0. If unknown, use the EXISTING proxy predicate and count the fallback. Apply this rule to all streams without selecting a market class from evaluation labels. Keep the row GRU and all 99 existing input features unchanged. For known rows, use direct transition deltas; do not rely on full-sequence mode anchoring in reconstruct(spreads=None), which examines later rows. No future maturity/target or invented timestamp enters inference.

cheap_discriminating_probe.scope: A decoder/clock feasibility audit only, no predictions or training.
cheap_discriminating_probe.sample: Freeze 16 pure validation sequences per fold by chain hash before scanning; report overall and class-3 descriptive slices without using class labels for the candidate routing. Compare existing AND-of-code-change mask with known decoded quote-move mask on every row; do not score only event snapshots.
measure: Known and unknown transition coverage by class and fold
Fraction of current proxy events that are known shape-only transitions
Known decoded price moves missed by the proxy
First-row/reset behavior and no-future prefix equivalence of the direct lookup
cheap_discriminating_probe.bounds: 2 CPU threads, 8 GiB, <=480 seconds, no GPU and no model fitting.
cheap_discriminating_probe.allocation: Only retain the route if train-only table provenance is verified, class-3 transition coverage >=99% in both folds and a clock disagreement affects >=1% of current proxy events in both folds. These are feasibility/materiality thresholds, not evidence of a score gain. Otherwise defer this exact implementation, without rejecting true event-clock modeling in general.
cheap_discriminating_probe.timeout_policy: On timeout record incomplete coverage and defer; no outcome-dependent resampling or assumption of zero unknown transitions.

preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.intervention: One fixed DualClockModel architecture/hyperparameter configuration copied from R6. Change only the event mask to the direct decoded/fallback rule; keep input features, dimensions, training rows, updates, losses, EMA and head FT identical.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.control: Same dual-clock model with current EV_I0PX. Compare additionally with ordinary row GRU and fixed C replacement; beating the old dual-clock negative alone is insufficient.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.outputs: Matched seed deltas, per-fold and pooled exact WP, across-seed SD, whole-chain conditional bootstrap. One predetermined C small-member replacement at .25 with all other members fixed; report decoder fallback metric-weight coverage.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.allocation_gate: A fixed C replacement must gain >=0.0005 pooled and be positive in both folds; both paired candidate-minus-proxy-clock seed effects must have positive pooled sign. This spending rule is discovery-only and cannot establish public improvement or causal mechanism.
preregistered_training_comparison_if_all.stop: One clock intervention; no decoder threshold, fallback, memory width, mixture coefficient or new horizon search after outcomes.

ranked_proposals.cost: Same recurrent parameter count, event branch updates may become fewer or more depending on measured disagreement. Additional causal code lookup and native decoder table are required; existing direct-predictor engine does not yet serve DualClockModel. Benchmark full one-core serving before promotion, or assess a separately registered same-size student only after teacher headroom. Do not claim zero cost or a deadline fit.
ranked_proposals.reason_ranked_second: The code reveals a real distinction, but strong previous dual-clock/attention negatives and decoder/export cost lower expected utility relative to the no-serving-cost head-FT study.
ranked_proposals.source_scope: Neural Hawkes is an example of event-conditioned recurrence, not evidence for this mask or a requirement to use a continuous-time process. This proposal uses observed row/code events only.

architecture_routes_not_allocated.reason: event_attn.py:63 and 85-88 store event content plus creation gap, with no explicit relative-event-age term in attention logits. Conditional on fixed query/key/value pairs, simultaneous token permutation leaves its weighted sum unchanged. However the row-GRU query and existing features are order-dependent, so the whole model is NOT order-blind. Dual-clock recurrence already keeps event order, and the Transformer has ALiBi. A positional tweak lacks sufficiently strong incremental evidence to outrank the training intervention.
architecture_routes_not_allocated.source_scope: Positional encoding in attention-only models; the applicability caveat for this recurrent-attention hybrid is essential.

architecture_routes_not_allocated.route: Generic wider GRU, LSTM, row convolution, separate i0/i1 towers, or more memory
architecture_routes_not_allocated.reason: Width audit M01 is unstable; LSTM E-081/E-168 negative, EMA row-conv E-181 negative, current two-stream pair -0.0004, periodic resets R1 negative, long-memory residual filters null and current Transformer fold0 reaches a similar fixed-recipe ceiling. These are recipe-specific negative results, not proof of an information-theoretic ceiling or a ban on all architectures.
